source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Once Pursat orange trees are fruiting, the program uses a 4-application fertilizer schedule timed to fruit development and paired with adequate irrigation throughout:

1) NPK 15-15-15 at 0.3-0.5 kg per tree, applied 1-2 months after fruit set (documented in the annual calendar as a February application).
2) NPK 15-15-15 at 0.3-0.5 kg per tree, applied again 3-4 months after fruit set (documented as an April application).
3) A third round is implied by the source's statement that 15-15-15 is applied on a roughly monthly basis for 3 rounds total during fruit development.
4) NPK 13-13-21 at 0.5-1.0 kg per tree, applied 1-2 months before harvest (documented as a June application, i.e. roughly 2 months ahead of the August-September harvest window).

The source explicitly notes that irrigation should follow immediately after each fertilizer application. The 13-13-21 blend used for the final, pre-harvest round is the custom-mixed formula described separately (see the NPK custom-blend mixing entry), since a ready-made 13-13-21 product is not available in Cambodia.
caveat: The narrative chapter (earlier in the source) describes this as '4 applications total' in a single paragraph without giving the 1-2 month / 3-4 month timing breakdown; the condensed month-by-month calendar table later in the same source gives that breakdown explicitly. Both are consistent on the fertilizer formulas and per-tree amounts; the calendar table is the source of the specific timing windows used here.
